dashboard.name: CoCoRaHS: Community Collaborative Rain, Hail and Snow Network
dashboard.data_archive: CoCoRaHS (Colorado State University); NOAA NCEI (copy in GHCN-Daily)
dashboard.update_status: Ongoing; daily reports, entered through the day as volunteers submit them.
dashboard.spatial_coverage: North America: U.S., Canada, Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands and the Bahamas
dashboard.temporal_frequency: Daily (plus event reports for hail and intense rain)
dashboard.curator: CoCoRaHS headquarters, Colorado Climate Center (Colorado State University)
dashboard.notes: Volunteer citizen-science network started in Colorado in 1998. About 28,000 observers read a standard 4-inch manual rain gauge at about 7 a.m. each day, and also report snowfall, snow depth and hail. Point observations, not gridded. The CoCoRaHS database is the archive of record; NOAA NCEI receives a daily stream into GHCN-Daily. No DOI or version number.

identification.doi_note: No DOI for the CoCoRaHS dataset itself. GHCN-Daily's DOI belongs to that separate product and should not be used for CoCoRaHS.
identification.data_provider: CoCoRaHS, Colorado Climate Center, Colorado State University
identification.description: A volunteer-based, citizen-science precipitation network started in Colorado in 1998. Observers measure rainfall, snowfall, snow depth and hail at their homes with standard manual equipment. The network is housed at the Colorado Climate Center at Colorado State University, and its observations are used by NOAA, the National Weather Service, researchers and hydrologists.

instruments.summary: Manual instruments read by volunteers; CoCoRaHS is not an automated weather-station network.

categories.name: Standard 4-inch diameter rain gauge
categories.role: Primary instrument: clear plastic gauge for liquid precipitation, read once each morning, in inches to hundredths

categories.name: Snowboard and snow ruler
categories.role: New snowfall and total snow depth; snow-water equivalent may also be reported

instruments.note: The standard CoCoRaHS precipitation observation is the manually read 4-inch rain gauge.

temporal.accumulation_period: About 24 hours, read around 7:00 a.m. local time
temporal.update_frequency: Daily, with reports submitted throughout the day
temporal.note: The main dataset is the daily precipitation observation for the preceding 24 hours. Hail, intense rainfall and other significant-weather reports are submitted when events happen, so they are not daily measurements.

other_frequencies.availability: Reports covering more than one day
Intense rainfall, hail and significant weather, when they happen

spatial.coverage: United States, Canada, Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands, the Bahamas and other participating locations
spatial.note: Point observations at volunteer stations, each with its own latitude and longitude. There is no fixed resolution: station spacing depends on where volunteers live, so it varies between rural and urban areas, and some places have several stations close together.

data_format.format: CSV, downloadable reports and web-based data products
data_format.units: Inches (metric available in the CSV export)

review_notes: Coverage is worded "North America: ..." so the dashboard tags it North America rather than CONUS (it has stations in Canada and the Bahamas).
The card's observer count (about 28,000) comes from Part 1 of the web research (cocorahs-about-pt1), not the Markdown.

Leads: the Markdown names Nolan Doesken (founder) and Henry Reges. Russ Schumacher was added from Part 3 (cocorahs-people-funding-pt3), which says CSU names him and Reges as the current leaders. Doesken's death on 15 November 2026 is from Part 4 (cocorahs-threats-news-pt4); check it.
Part 1 research also lists Guam among observer locations; the Markdown does not.
